title: capacity-smoothing-fix-and-emergency-replenish-for-reserved-pool-microburst-depletion
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers experienced degraded throughput and soft-throttles during adjacent region microbursts. Root cause analysis indicates the autoscaler smoothing window combined with the 'defer-warmup' safety gate suppressed scale-ups while a concurrent burst-credit reconciliation job drained headroom from the reserved pool. The net effect: a transient but severe reserved pool depletion and failed burst routing fallback for high-priority tenants.

Impact: High - multiple customer-facing timeouts and 3 enterprise escalations (Acct: BrightHealth, NovaSaaS, MarketEdge). Incidents manifested as 5-15s tail latency spikes and request rejections for burst candidates.

Immediate mitigation performed: manual headroom injection (+2 replicas) for affected pools, temporarily disabled smoothing gate, and forced fallback routing rules to prefer cold-pool warmups for VIP tenants. Contacted customers with interim remediation notes and apologized for impact.

Technical findings: 1) Smoothing logic (scaleController.SmoothWindow) uses decaying average that underweights sudden sustained bursts when combined with lease-ttl trimming; 2) Burst-credit reconciler batch job runs on a 30s cadence and performed a deferred write which caused headroom accounting to reflect lower available credit for 3 polling intervals; 3) Leader election jitter caused delayed scale-controller decisions in 2 AZs, compounding slow-up behavior.

Proposed short-term fix (hotfix): revert the aggressive smoothing factor for bursts (deploy runtime-1.23.0-hotfix), add a short-circuit path that allows an immediate 1x emergency replica if burst signal exceeds threshold and pool headroom below safety margin, and change reconciler backoff to staggered per-tenant writes to avoid simultaneous ledger updates.

Long-term work: rework smoothing algorithm to consider burst signal derivative and tenant priority, add deterministic unit/regression tests to cover microburst patterns, instrument end-to-end headroom telemetry and develop an autoscaler canary that simulates synthetic burst profiles nightly. Also enhance runbook to include a one-command headroom injection and automated customer notification hooks.

Artifacts: Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/playbooks/dedicated/reserved-pool-hot-inject
